anomalies.observed: Both VCAP pins of the STM32H753 (pins 48 and 73, power_out, the internal 1.2 V core regulator outputs) are routed to pins 3 and 4 of the UART3_FCC2 connector. No 2.2 µF VCAP capacitor is wired to either pin.
anomalies.expected: VCAP pins should go only to their own decoupling capacitors to GND. They should not reach an external connector, and UART3 pins 3 and 4 should carry UART signals on the MCU's USART pins.
anomalies.impact: The core-voltage regulator outputs are shorted to an external connector, so the H7 core rail is unstable or unpowered. The UART3 interface is also unusable.

anomalies.observed: The two VSS pins of the NAVC STM32F405 (pins 18 and 63) form their own net and are not connected to GND. The FCC2 MCU's VSS pins are all on GND.
anomalies.expected: All VSS pins of the MCU should return to the GND net, as the FCC2 VSS pins do.
anomalies.impact: The NAVC MCU has an isolated ground return, so its I/O levels and ADC references float relative to the rest of the board and the MCU is unreliable.

anomalies.observed: C4 (2.2 µF, 0603) has pin 1 on its own unconnected net. Only pin 2 reaches GND, so the capacitor does nothing.
anomalies.expected: A 2.2 µF capacitor in the FCC MCU decoupling or VCAP position should have both terminals connected, one to the supply or VCAP net and one to GND.
anomalies.impact: The capacitor is ineffective. If it was meant as the VCAP or supply decoupling, that supply lacks its bulk capacitance.

parsed.summary: The netlist shows the FCC MCU's VCAP outputs shorted to the UART3 connector, the NAVC MCU's VSS pins isolated from GND, and a 2.2 µF capacitor with one floating terminal. These connectivity faults are the most likely deviations, though the netlist is messy and some may be original design quirks.
